shortTitle: Agents that use screens and code
title: Agents that use screens and write code
hook: APIs first. Then screen control, code execution and coding assistants, each with its own risks.
inPlainWords: When there is no API, an agent can click through a screen like a person. When a task is really a calculation, an agent can write and run code. Both are powerful, and both need a locked room: limited access, no secrets, and review.

useCase.title: Reconcile 300 refunds against a carrier's website
useCase.story: A carrier's portal has no API. Each week someone types 300 tracking numbers to confirm delivery status, then builds a summary table by hand. It is dull, error-prone work.

approaches.name: Ask for an API or data feed
approaches.what: Get proper access to the data.

approaches.name: Screen-control agent
approaches.what: The agent reads and clicks through a website or app.
approaches.greatWhen: There is no API and volume is low.
approaches.avoidWhen: Pages change fast, or the account is sensitive.
approaches.example: Type tracking numbers into the portal.

approaches.name: Code-writing and running agent
approaches.what: The agent writes a script and runs it in a sandbox.
approaches.avoidWhen: Running code with real access and no review.
approaches.example: Build the weekly summary table with a script.

approaches.name: Coding assistant for engineers
approaches.what: AI suggests code, and a developer reviews it.
approaches.example: Draft a data collector, then a developer reviews it.

approaches.name: Recorded macros (RPA)
approaches.greatWhen: A stable screen and fixed steps.

approaches.name: Human in the loop
approaches.what: A person approves before anything changes.
approaches.greatWhen: Always for writes, payments and logins.
approaches.example: The agent proposes updates and a person approves.

challenge.question: The carrier has no API. What is the smartest design?

options.text: Ask for a data feed first. Otherwise use a sandboxed screen agent with a read-only account, limited credentials, logged actions, and human approval for any change
options.why: It is the least risky way to automate the job.

options.text: Give the agent your admin login and let it run
options.why: One mistake or trick could change real accounts.

options.text: Have the agent guess delivery statuses from memory
options.why: It has no way of knowing.

bestCase.title: Data feed first, then a locked-down agent with logs
bestCase.example: The carrier confirms no feed exists. A screen agent runs in a locked browser with a read-only account, reads statuses, and a sandboxed script builds the summary table. Every action is logged, and a person approves any update to ShopEase records.

worstCase.title: An agent with the keys to everything
worstCase.example: The agent uses a shared admin login on the live account. A misread button cancels 12 shipments, and there is no log of what it clicked.

steps.label: Sandboxed screen agent
steps.goes: It runs in a locked browser with a read-only account.
steps.goesWrong: The agent uses a shared admin login on the live account.

steps.label: Extract statuses
steps.goes: Delivery statuses are read into a table.

steps.label: Script builds the summary
steps.goes: Code runs in a sandbox with no secrets.

steps.label: Log every action
steps.goes: Every click and script run is recorded.

takeaway: Prefer real APIs. When you must use screens or code, lock the room: read-only access, no secrets, logs, and human approval for changes.
